idiom_name: Rails config.middleware insertion per environment / Sidekiq server middleware chain
implementation_notes: Rack stacks are the route: config.middleware.use, insert_before and delete in the environment file are how a Rails app switches a stage on or off, and Rack::Builder#use does the same outside Rails - the detour wraps the app callable and must call it so the message reaches the same destination. For job pipelines Sidekiq has the same construction: add or remove the middleware class from server_middleware in the initializer, and it wraps every job's perform; Sidekiq's chain API also supports explicit removal for exactly this purpose.
code_sketch:
# config/environments/staging.rb
Rails.application.configure do
  config.middleware.insert_before 0, AuditMiddleware if ENV['AUDIT_DETOUR'] == 'on'
end

class AuditMiddleware
  def initialize(app) = @app = app
  def call(env)
    tag_for_replay(env)   # inspect / modify the message
    @app.call(env)        # same destination on both legs
  end
end
pitfalls: Middleware is loaded once and not reloaded, so a config-level toggle needs a restart; for a live switch put the check inside call(env).
Rack middleware must call @app.call(env) and return its response - returning early turns the detour into a filter that silently changes routing.
Sidekiq keeps client and server middleware chains separate (a server that enqueues jobs is also a client), so a detour added to only one side never fires where you expect.
